minimum_execution_API_touchpoints.api: Versioned pidfd backend and lifecycle gate
minimum_contract: Use explicit local open_pidfd/send_pidfd functions, never monkeypatch os or signal and never fall back to numeric kill/killpg cleanup.

A reviewed architecture-specific syscall backend is feasible in principle on the recorded x86_64 system, but Python/libc API absence does not prove kernel syscall support. Actual capability remains unverified.
Fail closed on unsupported architecture, ENOSYS, permission/error conditions or failed ownership checks. Gate before attempt/output/lease side effects where possible.
Preserve parent-child ancestry, PID/start-tick checks before and after fd acquisition, fd-only signaling, subreaper/owned-descendant tracking, direct waits and complete drain evidence.
Both outer and inner supervisors must select the same validated backend; fixing the outer gate alone is insufficient.

response_to_parent: YES within the existing cooperative root-writer model and a narrow explicit instruction amendment, subject to all listed constraints. NO existing guard/API provides it today. It is not a source-preserving relaunch under original v4 execution authority.

revocation_boundary.defensible_condition: Root explicitly revokes all old cooperative project launch/write capabilities, certifies no old writers, and requires every newly authorized launch/write path to use the amendment gate. This matches the repository cooperative-root-writer trust boundary and does not claim hostile-process enforcement.
revocation_boundary.finding: A new authority file cannot make immutable old direct entrypoints enforce a predicate they never read. With the key still open, unchanged v3 remains an allocation checker, not an amendment selector.
revocation_boundary.stronger_requirement: If every frozen historical direct entrypoint must mechanically reject while remaining byte-identical and the allocation remains open, this proposal cannot satisfy that requirement without an additional enforcement layer or changing the applicable guard path.
